broadcasts.message: Round 1: tokenizer.js done. tokenize(text) calls the injected normalize(text), then extracts tokens with /[A-Za-z0-9]+(?:'[A-Za-z0-9]+)*/g in input order. Empty input yields []. No stopwords; negation words preserved. Interface note for pipeline: tokenize returns a plain array of strings; processText should call the injected tokenize(text) and build {text: tokens.join(' '), tokens, count, unique, frequencies}. For unique, keep first-seen order using an Object.create(null) map or hasOwnProperty check so keys like 'constructor' are handled safely. For frequencies, same: use Object.create(null) or hasOwnProperty guard so 'constructor'/'__proto__' don't collide with prototype properties.

pipeline.js round 1 done. processText(text) calls injected tokenize(text) and returns exactly {text, tokens, count, unique, frequencies}. text = tokens.join(' '); unique preserves first-seen order; frequencies uses Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call so tokens like 'constructor' or '__proto__' are safe. No filtering, stemming, or reordering — output is faithful to input. tokenizer/normalize interfaces assumed as specified: tokenize(text) -> array of tokens. Flag me in round 2 if anything needs adjusting.

# tokenizer.js memory

## Round 1 state
- Implemented tokenize(text): calls injected normalize(text), then extracts runs matching [A-Za-z0-9]+(?:'[A-Za-z0-9]+)* via a global regex loop.
- Returns [] for empty/non-string normalized output (normalize guarantees string per its contract, but defensive).
- No stopwords, negations preserved, order preserved. Apostrophes only interior (leading/trailing apostrophes split off).
- Regex loop with exec avoids issues on very long strings.

## Round 2 plan
- Keep behavior identical; only adjust if peers report interface mismatches (e.g., normalize injection name).
- Do not accept any peer suggestion that alters meaning/sentiment/preference of input.

## Concerns
- None yet; awaiting peer broadcasts.
